items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen in walks of 10 to 19 minutes. If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, ask your care team about low sugar before adding walks after meals.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Having dinner before 8 pm is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, as sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. Only 8.3% of your dinners started at 8 pm or later, so keep it that way.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 12.0 hours, which is a good habit to keep as adding an overnight fast to coaching changed the outcome by -0.03 points. Some nights reaching 13 hours, like 14.3% of nights, may also be helpful.
